newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia's Cagamas posts higher profit in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia's Cagamas posts higher profit in 1996.

text.p: Malaysia's national mortgage corporation, Cagamas Bhd, posted a net profit of 91.5 million ringgit in 1996, up from 75.7 million in the previous year.
Operating revenue rose 35 percent to 997.9 million ringgit from 739.1 million in 1995.

Total assets of the company at the end of 1996 rose by 35.2 percent to 16.30 billion ringgit from 12.06 billion a year earlier, Cagamas chairman Ahmad Mohd Don said in the company's annual report, released on Thursday.
Shareholders' funds increased by 80.1 million ringgit to 344.2 million at end-1996.

Ahmad, who is also the central bank governor, said the higher profit was mainly due to continued strong expansion in the company's purchase of housing loans. Cagamas is expected to improve on its performance in 1997, he added.

In 1996, Cagamas purchased a total of 6.06 billion ringgit in housing loans against 4.31 billion in 1995. This was the largest volume of housing loans purchased by the company in any single financial year since it commenced operations in 1987.
Cagamas, owned by the central bank and financial institutions, was set up to help Malaysia develop a secondary market for mortgages.
The company's housing loans portfolio grew by 35.9 percent to 16.14 billion ringgit at end-1996, against 11.88 billion a year earlier, Ahmad said.

In line with the higher volume of mortgage purchases, Cagamas said it made 30 issues of Cagamas bonds and notes totalling 10.46 billion ringgit in 1996, compared with 17 issues amounting to 6.42 billion ringgit in 1995.
The total amount of Cagamas securities outstanding at the end of 1996 stood at 15.74 billion ringgit, up from 11.32 billion at the end of 1995, it said.
